question: A 6-month-old boy is brought to the physician for a well-child examination. The boy was born at term, and the pregnancy was complicated by prolonged labor. There is no family history of any serious illnesses. He can sit upright but needs help to do so and cannot roll over from the prone to the supine position. He can pull himself to stand. He can grasp his rattle and can transfer it from one hand to the other. He babbles. He cries if anyone apart from his parents holds him or plays with him. He touches his own reflection in the mirror. Vital signs are within normal limits. He is at the 40th percentile for head circumference, 30th percentile for length, and 40th percentile for weight. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. Which of the following developmental milestones is delayed in this infant?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "6-month-old boy" -> "can sit upright with help" -> "cannot roll over from prone to supine" -> "gross motor milestone of rolling over is delayed" -> 85%
CHAIN: "6-month-old boy" -> "can pull himself to stand" -> "can grasp and transfer rattle" -> "fine motor skills are appropriate for age" -> 90%
CHAIN: "6-month-old boy" -> "babbles" -> "language development is appropriate for age" -> 90%
CHAIN: "6-month-old boy" -> "cries when held by others" -> "shows attachment to parents" -> "social development is appropriate for age" -> 90%
CHAIN: "6-month-old boy" -> "touches own reflection" -> "demonstrates some cognitive awareness" -> "cognitive development is appropriate for age" -> 90%
analysis: The infant is 6 months old and is able to sit upright with assistance, pull himself to stand, grasp and transfer objects, and babble. However, he cannot roll over from prone to supine, which is a gross motor milestone typically achieved by 6 months of age. Therefore, the gross motor milestone is delayed.
